messages.subject: Re: plotting list object using ggplot
parts:
Hi:

Here's one attempt; note that the ggplot() function generally takes
data frames as input, so the data manipulation game is to produce a
data frame out of the vectors of simulated success proportions. It is
then 'melted' using the reshape2 package and the melted data frame is
passed to ggplot(). The purpose of melting is to create a factor
variable whose levels are the sample size strings, since they are the
labels you want for the facets in facet_wrap() below.

N <- 8619170
nn <- c(1000, 1200, 3000)
p <- .27
nsim <- 100

# This works because a data frame is a special case of a list object
DF <- data.frame(lapply(nn, function(n) rhyper(nsim, N * p, N * (1 - p), n)/n))
names(DF) <- paste("n =", nn)

library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)
DFm <- melt(DF)

ggplot(DFm, aes(x = value)) +
geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.001) +
theme_bw() +
geom_vline(xintercept = 0.27, color = "red", linetype = "longdash") +
facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol = 1) +
labs(x = "Success proportion", y = "Frequency")

Dennis
